newsitem.title: USA: US Senate votes to end aid if Korean armistice broken.
newsitem.headline: US Senate votes to end aid if Korean armistice broken.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Wednesday unanimously voted to halt additional U.S. economic aid to North Korea if the country again violated its armistice agreement with South Korea.

Sen. Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, won approval for an amendment to a foreign spending bill that orders the president to certify that North Korea is in compliance with the armistice for nine months prior to any additional aid.
North Korea on Wednesday fired artillery shells at a Southern guard post in one of the worst border clashes in recent years, Seoul military officials said.

The Senate amendment withholds an additional $14 million in aid to the Korean Economic Development Organisation proposed by the Clinton administration in the fiscal 1998 budget, but does not affect $30 million in aid called for under the terms of the an October 1994 framework agreement with North Korea, Murkowski said.

"We should be outraged at North Korea's continued belligerent actions that are clearly designed to intimidate," Murkowski said in a statement. "If the North Koreans want economic assistance from the United States they are going to have to learn that their troops and their munitions ought to stay on their side of the border."
He cited a General Accounting Office report that Washington has sent more than $115 million in food and economic aid to North Korea since the "agreed framework" agreement was signed.
The United States on Tuesday pledged an additional $27 million in food aid to North Korea, bringing to $52 million its contribution for the year.
